title: September 2019 Class Block 3 Supplementary College Final Exam (Part 3 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Psychology, Sociology, Growth and Development, Nursing Process, Medical-Surgical Nursing, Respiratory, Cardiovascular, Renal, Endocrine, Reproductive Health, Oncology and Neurology)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class Block 3 Supplementary College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 6 December 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q41 to Q60).

questions.text: A defense mechanism that involves diverting libidinal diverting energy from sex object to more social acceptable activity is: -
questions.explanation: Sublimation (A) is correct because it is the redirecting of unacceptable (sexual or aggressive) drives into socially acceptable activities, such as sport, art or work. Projection (B) is incorrect because it is attributing one's own unacceptable feelings or thoughts to another person. Displacement (C) is incorrect because it is transferring feelings from the real object to a safer, substitute object (for example shouting at a spouse after being scolded by the boss), without turning the energy into an approved activity. Rationalization (D) is incorrect because it is giving logical or socially acceptable reasons to justify behaviour or to explain away a disappointment.

questions.text: The average increase per month of weight of and infant is: -
questions.explanation: 300-600 grams (C) is correct as the best answer because an infant gains about 150 to 200 grams a week in the first 3 to 6 months (about 600 to 800 grams a month), which slows to about 70 to 90 grams a week (300 to 400 grams a month) in the second half of the first year, so the average over infancy is in the range of 300 to 600 grams a month. 150-200 grams (A) is incorrect because this is the weekly gain in the early months, and not the monthly gain. 250-290 grams (B) is incorrect because it is too low and too narrow for the average. 700-1000 grams (D) is incorrect because it is higher than the usual gain even in the fastest-growing months. Note: the figure depends on the age of the infant, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: One of the following is enhanced in the values of a social group and violation attracts intense social reaction: -
questions.explanation: Mores (B) is correct because mores are strongly held norms that are central to the values of a group and regarded as essential to its welfare (for example taboos against incest, murder and theft), so violating them brings strong social disapproval, punishment or expulsion. Symbolic culture (A) is incorrect because it is the non-material part of culture (language, symbols, beliefs). Folkway (C) is incorrect because it is a customary everyday norm (such as table manners) whose violation brings only mild reactions like ridicule or gossip. Sanction (D) is incorrect because it is the reward or punishment used to enforce a norm, and not the norm itself.

questions.text: The type of assessment that the midwife should conduct on a normal newborn immediately after delivery is: -
questions.explanation: Comprehensive (C) is correct as the best answer because the midwife makes a full assessment of the normal newborn soon after delivery, including the Apgar score, a complete head-to-toe examination, measurement of weight, length and head circumference, and checks for abnormalities, to establish a baseline. Emergency (A) is incorrect because it is a rapid assessment to find and treat life-threatening problems, and the newborn is normal. Focused (B) is incorrect because it looks at a specific problem or body system, for example follow-up of a known condition. Time-lapsed (D) is incorrect because it is a reassessment done after a period to compare with previous findings. Note: a focused or initial rapid assessment is done in the first minutes, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: The planning component of nursing process involves: -

options.A: Assigning priorities, formulation of nursing diagnosis
options.B: Developing expected outcomes, outlining nursing activities
options.C: Developing nursing diagnosis, analysis of collected data

questions.explanation: Developing expected outcomes, outlining nursing activities (B) is correct because planning includes setting priorities, writing goals and expected outcomes, selecting nursing interventions and documenting the care plan. Assigning priorities, formulation of nursing diagnosis (A) is incorrect because the formulation of the nursing diagnosis belongs to the diagnosis step. Developing nursing diagnosis, analysis of collected data (C) is incorrect because both belong to the diagnosis step. Processing data, developing expected outcomes (D) is incorrect because processing (organising and analysing) data belongs to the assessment and diagnosis steps.

questions.text: An appropriate diagnostic label for a patient with, respiratory rate of 28breaths/min, shortness of breath and use of accessory muscles is: -
questions.explanation: Ineffective breathing pattern (C) is correct because the defining characteristics are a changed rate (tachypnoea of 28 breaths per minute), dyspnoea and use of accessory muscles, which show that inspiration or expiration is not giving adequate ventilation. Impaired gas exchange (A) is incorrect because it is defined by findings such as hypoxia, hypercapnia, cyanosis and abnormal blood gases, which are not given. Ineffective airway clearance (B) is incorrect because it is defined by an inability to clear secretions, with cough, abnormal breath sounds and sputum. Altered oxygenation (D) is incorrect because it is not a standard NANDA nursing diagnosis label.

questions.text: Nurse P performs change of wound dressing on a patient, at the end of the shift she realizes that she documented on the wrong patient notes. The next appropriate action is: -

options.A: Complete an occurrence report before leaving
options.B: Write the note of the dressing change into an earlier note
options.C: Use a white out to delete wrong entry
options.D: Draw a straight line on the note and sign.

questions.explanation: Draw a straight line on the note and sign (D) is correct because an erroneous entry is corrected by drawing a single line through it so that it remains legible, writing 'wrong entry' or 'mistaken entry' with the date, time and signature, and then writing the information in the correct patient's notes. Complete an occurrence report before leaving (A) is incorrect as the next step because the record must first be corrected, although an incident report may follow according to the hospital policy. Write the note of the dressing change into an earlier note (B) is incorrect because inserting entries into earlier notes is falsification of records. Use a white out to delete wrong entry (C) is incorrect because correction fluid or erasing hides the original entry and is not allowed in legal records.

questions.text: Appropriate health message to give a mother of a child who has had tympanostomy tube (grommet) inserted is to: -

options.B: Remove the tube after 1 week of insertion
options.C: Avoid the child lying on the affected ear

questions.explanation: Observe for premature tube extrusion (D) is correct because the grommet normally comes out by itself after about 6 to 12 months, so the mother is taught to watch for early extrusion (the tube seen in the ear canal or on the pillow), to report any ear discharge or pain, to keep water out of the ear, and to attend follow-up so that hearing can be checked. Irrigate the ear once daily (A) is incorrect because irrigation can introduce infection and is avoided. Remove the tube after 1 week of insertion (B) is incorrect because the tube is left in place until it extrudes or is removed by the ENT specialist. Avoid the child lying on the affected ear (C) is incorrect because positioning on the ear is not restricted, although discharge is wiped away.

questions.text: Nasal congestion, snoring, halitosis are manifestations of: -
questions.explanation: Adenoiditis (B) is correct because enlarged, inflamed adenoids block the nasopharynx, so the child has nasal congestion and obstruction, mouth breathing, snoring, bad breath (halitosis), a nasal voice, and often ear problems. Tonsillitis (A) is incorrect because it presents with a sore throat, painful swallowing, fever and red, swollen tonsils. Laryngitis (C) is incorrect because it presents with hoarseness or loss of voice. Rhino-sinusitis (D) is incorrect as the best answer because it presents with facial pain or pressure, purulent nasal discharge and headache, although nasal congestion occurs.

questions.text: The correct chest compression: ventilation ratio in 2- rescuer CPR for a five-year-old is: -
questions.explanation: 15:2 (B) is correct because for children (and infants) when there are two health-care rescuers, the ratio is 15 compressions to 2 breaths, whereas a single rescuer uses 30:2. 30:2 (A) is incorrect because it is the ratio for adults and for a single rescuer on a child. 2:30 (C) and 2:15 (D) are incorrect because they put the breaths first, and the compression:ventilation ratio always starts with compressions.

questions.text: Wheezing in a patient with acute asthmatic attack is due to: -
questions.explanation: Bronchospasm of the lower airway (C) is correct because in an asthma attack the smooth muscle of the bronchi contracts, with mucosal oedema and mucus, narrowing the small airways, so air flowing through them (especially on expiration) produces a high-pitched whistling sound called wheeze. Inflammation of lung parenchyma (A) is incorrect because it describes pneumonia, with crackles and bronchial breathing. Edema of the larynx (B) is incorrect because it causes stridor, an upper airway sound. Collapse of alveoli (D) is incorrect because it describes atelectasis, with reduced breath sounds.

questions.text: The nursing responsibilities for Mrs. Bee, diagnosed with right sided- heart failure include: -

options.D: Encouraging active exercises, promoting salt intake

questions.explanation: Monitoring body weight, administering diuretics (A) is correct because right-sided heart failure causes systemic venous congestion, with peripheral oedema, ascites and weight gain, so the nurse weighs the patient daily to assess fluid retention, gives diuretics as prescribed, and also restricts salt and fluids and monitors the intake and output. Commencing oxygen, Administering mucolytic (B) is incorrect because mucolytics are for productive cough in lung disease, though oxygen can be needed. Discontinuing antihypertensive, administering fluids (C) is incorrect because fluids would worsen the overload, and antihypertensives are not stopped. Encouraging active exercises, promoting salt intake (D) is incorrect because the patient is given rest and a low-salt diet.

questions.text: Mr. Gee develops neck vein distension, muffled heart sounds and blood pressure of 90/40mmHg following open heart surgery. The nurse suspects: -
questions.explanation: Cardiac tamponade (B) is correct because bleeding or fluid in the pericardial sac after cardiac surgery compresses the heart and stops it from filling, giving Beck's triad: distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds and hypotension (with a narrow pulse pressure and pulsus paradoxus); it is an emergency that needs urgent notification of the surgeon and pericardiocentesis or re-exploration. Cardiomyopathy (A) is incorrect because it is a chronic disease of the heart muscle, and does not appear suddenly after surgery with this triad. Heart failure (C) is incorrect because it would give crackles in the lungs, a third heart sound and oedema, not muffled heart sounds. Postural hypotension (D) is incorrect because it does not cause distended neck veins or muffled heart sounds.

questions.text: Clinical features of nephrotic syndrome include: -
questions.explanation: Peri orbital edema, proteinuria (C) is correct because in nephrotic syndrome the glomerular membrane leaks protein, causing heavy proteinuria (more than 3.5 g a day in adults), low serum albumin, hyperlipidaemia and generalised oedema that is first seen around the eyes in the morning. Fever, pyuria (A) is incorrect because they are features of urinary tract infection. Lower abdominal pain, abdominal distention (B) is incorrect because they suggest urinary retention or bowel conditions, although ascites can occur in severe cases. Urine retention, weight loss (D) is incorrect because the patient has reduced urine output with weight gain from fluid retention, not weight loss.

questions.text: The recommended definitive treatment for chronic renal failure is: -
questions.explanation: Renal transplant (C) is correct because it is the definitive treatment of end-stage renal failure, as the new kidney takes over the function of the failed kidneys and gives better survival and quality of life than dialysis. Hemodialysis (A) and Peritoneal dialysis (B) are incorrect because they are renal replacement therapies that only replace part of the kidney function, and are used to support the patient until transplant, or lifelong if transplant is not possible. Protein restriction (D) is incorrect because it is a dietary measure that slows the build-up of urea and the progression of the disease, and is not a definitive treatment.

questions.text: The nursing intervention of Mrs. Z diagnosed with hypothyroidism includes: -

options.A: Administration of propranolol 10mg per oral 8 hourly
options.C: Administration of levothyroxine 50 mcg per once daily
options.D: Maintaining active exercises three times a day

questions.explanation: Administration of levothyroxine 50 mcg once daily (C) is correct because hypothyroidism is treated with lifelong thyroid hormone replacement with levothyroxine, started at a low dose (for example 25 to 50 mcg) in the morning on an empty stomach, and increased gradually according to the TSH. Administration of propranolol 10mg 8 hourly (A) is incorrect because beta-blockers are used to control the symptoms (tachycardia, tremor) of hyperthyroidism. Preparing the patient for thyroidectomy (B) is incorrect because thyroidectomy is a treatment of hyperthyroidism or thyroid cancer. Maintaining active exercises three times a day (D) is incorrect because the hypothyroid patient is fatigued with a slow metabolism, and activity is increased gradually as tolerated, so scheduled active exercise is not the priority intervention.

questions.text: Azoospermia is: -

options.A: Complete absence of sperm in semen
options.B: A sperm count of less than 15 million / ml of semen
options.D: A sperm count of more than 15 million / ml of semen

questions.explanation: Complete absence of sperm in semen (A) is correct because azoospermia means that there are no sperm at all in the ejaculate, which can be due to a blockage (obstructive) or to failure of sperm production (non-obstructive). A sperm count of less than 15 million/ml (B) is incorrect because it describes oligospermia. Reduced sperm motility in semen (C) is incorrect because it describes asthenospermia. A sperm count of more than 15 million/ml (D) is incorrect because it is within the normal range.

questions.text: Mrs. B ,58 years old presents with post-menopausal bleeding for the past two weeks, the appropriate diagnostic investigation would be: -
questions.explanation: Endometrium biopsy (D) is correct because post-menopausal bleeding must be assumed to be endometrial cancer until it is proved otherwise, and it is investigated with an endometrial biopsy (or dilatation and curettage or hysteroscopy), usually together with a transvaginal ultrasound to measure the endometrial thickness. Colposcopy (A) is incorrect because it examines the cervix after an abnormal Pap smear. Cone biopsy (B) is incorrect because it is used to diagnose and treat cervical precancer. Pap smear (C) is incorrect because it screens for cervical cancer and does not sample the endometrium reliably.

questions.text: “B symptoms” in Lymphoma include: -

options.C: Headache, enlarged liver, tender lymph nodes
options.D: Recurrent fever, night sweats, weight loss

questions.explanation: Recurrent fever, night sweats, weight loss (D) is correct because the B symptoms of lymphoma are unexplained fever (above 38 degrees Celsius), drenching night sweats and loss of more than 10% of body weight over 6 months, and they indicate more advanced disease and a worse outlook in the Ann Arbor staging. Pruritus, painless lymphadenopathy, night sweats (A) is incorrect because pruritus and painless lymph nodes are common presenting features, but they are not B symptoms. Abdominal pain, bone pain, fever (B) is incorrect because abdominal and bone pain are not B symptoms. Headache, enlarged liver, tender lymph nodes (C) is incorrect because none of these is a B symptom.

questions.text: Manifestations of Secondary brain injury includes: -

options.A: Fracture of the occipital bone, epidural hematoma

questions.explanation: Cerebral edema, increased intracranial pressure (B) is correct because secondary brain injury is the damage that develops hours to days after the initial impact, as a result of cerebral oedema, raised intracranial pressure, hypoxia, ischaemia, hypotension and infection. Fracture of the occipital bone, epidural hematoma (A) is incorrect because a fracture is a primary injury (direct impact) and an epidural haematoma is a primary focal injury, even if it can enlarge later. Raccoons eye, intracerebral edema (C) is incorrect because raccoon eyes (periorbital bruising) is a sign of a primary basal skull fracture. Hallo sign, intracerebral edema (D) is incorrect because the halo sign (ring of fluid around blood on a gauze) is a sign of a primary basal skull fracture with CSF leak.
